To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the learnability of any language in a family is independent of the learnability of the family itself; (2) monotonic learning is equivalent to learning of the whole target language; (3) learning of the whole language implies learning of any language in the family; (4) the learnability in the limit implies monotonicity of learning in the limit; (5) the learnability under monotonicity constraint implies the learnability of whole languages in the limit; and

the following language families are not learnable in the limit by a monotonic learner: (i) all languages in NP, (ii) all languages in P, (iii) all languages in L, and (iv) the language of all palindromes.
